title: Derived category homology commutes with coefficient extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category with identity-cover topology, let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and use the constant-ring module categories, maps $\pi_{\mathcal E}^R,\pi_{\mathcal E}^S$ and bar complexes of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. Let $h:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\underline S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),\underline R)$ and $f:(*,S)\to(*,R)$ be the ringed-topos morphisms with identity underlying topoi and structural maps $R\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Derived extension of scalars means $Lh^*(-)=-\otimes_{\underline R}^{\mathbf L}\underline S$ and $Lf^*(-)=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every bounded-above complex $M$ of $\underline R$-modules there is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^S(M\otimes_{\underline R}^{\mathbf L}\underline S)\ \simeq\ (L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S.$$
For a presheaf $F$ whose every value $F(U)$ is a flat $R$-module (flat means tensoring with it preserves short exact sequences), the derived presheaf tensor may be replaced by $F\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S$, and this isomorphism is represented by the termwise identification
$$K_{\mathcal E}(F\otimes_R S)\cong K_{\mathcal E}(F)\otimes_R S,\qquad (U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x\otimes s)\longleftrightarrow(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\otimes s.$$
Here $K_{\mathcal E}(F)$ is a bounded-above complex of flat $R$-modules, so $K_{\mathcal E}(F)\otimes_R S$ computes the derived tensor on the right. These isomorphisms are compatible with maps of module presheaves, functors between small indexing categories, and commutative squares of coefficient-ring maps, using the semilinear derived-colimit maps of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $T_{\mathcal E}=Lh^*$, $T_*=Lf^*$, and $r_{\mathcal E},r_*$ for scalar restriction. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], $T_{\mathcal E}\dashv r_{\mathcal E}$ and $T_*\dashv r_*$, with their tensor-unit normalization. Let $L_R=L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R$ and $L_S=L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^S$. By [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar], $L_R\dashv C_R$, $L_S\dashv C_S$. The equality $r_{\mathcal E}C_S=C_Rr_*$ holds on objects, actions, maps and differentials: each side is the same constant underlying $R$-complex [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

Compose these adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Put $A=L_ST_{\mathcal E}$, $B=T_*L_R$ and $V=r_{\mathcal E}C_S=C_Rr_*$. For every $M$ and $N\in D(S)$ the two composite Hom bijections identify $\operatorname{Hom}(AM,N)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(BM,N)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(M,VN)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] there is a unique natural isomorphism $\chi:A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ with $V(\chi_M)\eta_{A,M}=\eta_{B,M}$. This applies in particular to bounded-above $M$; its inverse satisfies $V(\chi_M^{-1})\eta_{B,M}=\eta_{A,M}$, the normalization required in step 3.

source.place: Tag 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings), with the typed order and left-adjoint direction corrected.

proof.text: For objectwise flat $F$, apply [lem-trf-objectwise-flat-bar-kflat]: $F[0]$ and $K_R(F)$ have flat terms and are K-flat, and their ordinary scalar tensors compute both derived extensions. The bar theorem [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] represents the left side by $K_S(F\otimes_R S)$. Apply [lem-trf-bar-scalar-unit-transpose] to these models: its $\beta_F$ is represented by $\Phi_F^{-1}$ and has the common-adjunction unit normalization. By uniqueness [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], $\beta_F=\chi_F^{-1}$. Thus $\chi_F$ is represented by $(\sigma,x\otimes s)\mapsto(\sigma,x)\otimes s$, as claimed.

source.place: Tags 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), 08PH (example-morphism-categories), 08Q8 (lemma-change-of-rings); extracted flat-model and transpose arguments.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-colimit-scalar-coherence] to the normalized comparisons just constructed. Its derived exchange square gives compatibility with module maps, indexing functors and arbitrary commutative coefficient squares, including identities and composites. Its chain square sends each generator to $(u\sigma,t(x))\otimes b(s)$, so step 3 identifies the explicit compatibility with this same derived compatibility. All three extracted statements allow arbitrary coefficient-ring maps, so no flatness of $S$ over $R$ is used.
